claims.text: LPBF-fabricated AlCoCrFeNiMn is a two-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy.
A critical interphase-boundary spacing maximizes tensile strength in LPBF-fabricated AlCoCrFeNiMn.
A critical interphase-boundary spacing maximizes hardness in LPBF-fabricated AlCoCrFeNiMn.
Below the critical interphase-boundary spacing, Hall–Petch-type strengthening dominates.
Above the critical interphase-boundary spacing, dislocation multiplication causes softening.
LPBF's high cooling rates can refine EHEA microstructures.
Systematically varying LPBF cooling rates can produce a controlled series of interphase-boundary spacings.
Supplemental thermal treatments can be used to control interphase-boundary spacing while retaining the intended eutectic system.
Decreasing a characteristic microstructural scale generally increases strength through Hall–Petch strengthening until nanoscale breakdown occurs.
Interphase-boundary spacing directly governs both hardness and tensile strength in the proposed alloy.
Samples near the critical spacing will have greater tensile strength than samples with substantially larger spacing.
Samples near the critical spacing will have greater tensile strength than samples with substantially smaller spacing.
Samples near the critical spacing will have greater hardness than samples with substantially larger or smaller spacing.
Below the critical spacing, dislocation-multiplication-mediated softening can replace Hall–Petch strengthening.
Formation of non-equilibrium phases or excessive coarsening may invalidate the proposed spacing–strength mechanism.
Failure to observe a statistically significant intermediate-spacing peak in tensile strength and hardness would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis assigns Hall–Petch strengthening to spacings below the critical value, which would ordinarily predict continued strengthening as spacing decreases, but the predicted outcome says substantially smaller spacings are weaker. The cited evidence instead places dislocation-multiplication-mediated softening below the critical spacing.
